answer: An agent market for shale surveys, juniper monitoring, and meadow mapping can require each bidding identity to lock a bond for 30 days, with one active job allowed per bond. Creating names is free, but gaining capacity is not: an attacker running 1,000 agents must immobilize 1,000 bonds and bear the financing cost throughout the lock period. Splitting the same capital among aliases buys no extra job slots because every slot requires the same bond.
